newsitem.title: MEXICO: JP Morgan revises up '96 Mexico inflation forecast.
newsitem.headline: JP Morgan revises up '96 Mexico inflation forecast.

text.p: U.S.-based investment bank J.P. Morgan on Monday revised up its 1996 forecast for Mexican inflation to 27 percent from 26.3 percent based on the 1997 economic plan, or "pacto", reached by the government, business and labor.

The pacto set a 17 percent increase in the minimum wage for 1997, higher than the 15 percent that was widely expected, J.P. Morgan said. Plus, public-sector prices for gasoline and electricity also are seeing steeper-than-expected increases.

"Given the higher-than-expected rises in these items contained in the actual agreement, the end-year 1996 CPI inflation forecast has been raised to 27 percent from 26.3 percent previously," analyst Alfredo Thorne wrote.
The adjustment applies to the CPI for November and December, Thorne said.
J.P. Morgan's November inflation forecast moves to 1.8 percent from 1.6 percent and the December forecast to 2.3 percent from 1.9 percent.
Cumulative inflation for the first nine months of this year was 20.39 percent, according to Banco de Mexico.
